overlap_rationale: Study A (S309: Hernandez, Manuel-Navarrete, Lerner & Siqueiros 2023, International Journal of the Commons) has no accessible full text in the audit packet ([FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE — NO VERIFIED FULL-TEXT PDF COULD BE RETRIEVED]). Study B (S676: Hernández Aguilar, Lerner, Manuel-Navarrete & Siqueiros-García 2021, Water International) has a complete, readable 20-page full text examining water supply narratives in two informal settlements in Xochimilco, Mexico City (Amplicación Tizilclipa and San José Obrero) based on 27 semi-structured key-informant interviews (2017–2019) and 41 resident questionnaires (2018–2019). Although the citation metadata of Study A shares the same core research team (Hernández, Manuel-Navarrete, Lerner and Siqueiros) and general geographic setting (informal areas of Xochimilco, Mexico City), it cannot be verified without Study A's full text whether S309 analyses the exact same 2017–2019 fieldwork sample in Amplicación Tizilclipa and San José Obrero, a partially overlapping sample, or distinct data collection. Per strict audit rules, pair_classification, same_underlying_data, and synthesis_double_counting_risk are set to cannot_tell.
study_a_sample_and_data: Full text not accessible ([FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE — NO VERIFIED FULL-TEXT PDF COULD BE RETRIEVED]). From metadata alone, S309 is a 2023 International Journal of the Commons article on informal water distribution, collective agency and self-organization in informal areas of Xochimilco, Mexico City; specific settlements, fieldwork dates, sample size (N) and empirical methods cannot be verified.
study_b_sample_and_data: Two informal settlements in the southern Conservation Zone of Xochimilco municipality, Mexico City (Amplicación Tizilclipa and San José Obrero). Data collected in 2017 (semi-structured interviews with government officials) and 2018–2019 (community leaders and residents), comprising N = 27 key-informant semi-structured interviews (17 community/parada leaders, 5 local Alcaldía government officials/piperos, and 3 Mexico City government officials from SACMEX, CORENA and SEDEMA) plus N = 41 resident questionnaires (20 in San José Obrero and 21 in Amplicación Tizilclipa), coded in MAXQDA 2018.
